summary: Replace deprecated chunking round-trip with generation-aware source confirmation
description:
tests/test_chunking.py::test_round_trip is now @pytest.mark.skip DEPRECATED. Its
docstring carries the full write-up; this ticket tracks the replacement.

## Why it was unsound

It asserted stored chunk bodies are findable in the *current* raw. That only
holds while corpus and raw were produced by the same generation of the
pipeline. They are not: acquisition now strips footnotes, so chunks built
before that change retain footnote paragraphs the raw no longer contains.

Clearest case — mandaean.gnostic-john-baptizer-2.008 is a footnote block
("1 Presumably the Seven. 2 Presumably the End-Sea. ...") present in NO raw
file: not the uncleaned raw, not the clean_body-normalized raw. It cannot be
found because it is not there.

The old test had accumulated epicycles: apparatus-chunk skips, an advisory
tolerance for paragraphs <=60 chars, per-page pre_strip mirroring, a raw-side
clean_body call. Each was a real patch for a real divergence, and each widened
the tolerance until the test could only fail on cases it had not yet been
taught to excuse. A test that must mirror every transform in the pipeline is
testing the mirror.

## Scope (measured 2026-08-08)

3 chunks across 2 texts, both mandaean/gnostic-john-baptizer-2 and -3. Narrow —
a design problem, not a corpus emergency.

## What to build

The invariant is worth keeping: no invented content, no reordering in stored
chunk bodies. Only the formulation is wrong.

1. Compare at WORD level rather than paragraph level — assert the body's word
   sequence appears as an in-order subsequence of the raw's, scanning
   monotonically. Any deletion-only transform (footnote stripping, [Pg N]
   markers, nav) is then tolerated by construction while invented content and
   reordering still fail. Subsequence matching alone is too permissive, so
   guard it: require contiguous runs of N words, or a coverage threshold over
   substantive sentences.

2. Record the acquisition generation a corpus was built against — a hash or
   timestamp in corpus/*/metadata.toml against raw/*.meta.toml — so a mismatch
   reports "stale raw: re-acquire or re-chunk" instead of "invented content".
   That distinction is the actual bug this failure was trying to report, and
   the reason it was misread for so long.

## Separate decision

Whether the 2 mandaean texts should simply be re-chunked against current raw is
a corpus call, not a test one. Doing that would make the old test pass without
fixing its formulation, so it is not a substitute for the above.
